channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Revela'T 2027 Open Call for Projects — Timeless
item.description: Three analog photography projects are produced or transported and exhibited at the 15th Revela'T festival near Barcelona in September 2027, with up to €1,000, €500 and €500 toward production plus travel, two nights' lodging and a full pass. Open to any nationality working in film or photochemical processes; 10–15 images per project. — Deadline: December 20, 2026. Fee: €22 (€11 Revela'T Friends). Prize: Exhibition + €1,000 production + Accommodation.

item.title: MONOCHROME: Light, Form, & Tone · PhotoPlace Gallery
item.description: Susan Burnstine will choose up to 35 photographs for the Middlebury gallery show and about 40 more for the online gallery, with every selection reproduced in the exhibition catalog and archived permanently on the site. Any monochromatic work qualifies, from black and white and sepia to cyanotype or a single dominant tone. Entry is $39 for five images. — Deadline: December 7, 2026. Fee: $39 (5 images) + $6 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: Off Raw Photo Fest 2027 — Exhibition Open Call · The Raw Society
item.description: The Raw Society's new Menorca festival will hang 39 photographers in Alaior from 15 March to 15 April 2027, with production costs covered and inclusion in Issue VI of its magazine. Open worldwide to anyone 18 or over working in street, documentary or travel photography; single images only. — Deadline: January 17, 2027. Fee: €15 per image, €60 for 5 (20% member discount). Prize: Exhibition + Magazine feature.

item.title: Yaddo Residency — Winter 2026 Cycle
item.description: Yaddo's winter cycle covers two-week to two-month residencies starting May 2027 through March 2028 at its Saratoga Springs estate, with room, board and a private studio; photography is one of ten disciplines. The portal opens 20 November and closes at 1,600 applications or 20 December, whichever comes first. — Deadline: December 20, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Homo Technologicus — Issue Collective #5 · LoosenArt
item.description: LoosenArt's call for Issue Collective #5 asks photographers, video makers and digital designers for work on the relationship between humans and technology — social, environmental, cognitive and emotional. Entry is free and worldwide, one to three works each; publication is the outcome, and a further selection may join a 2027 group show in Milan, Rome or Cagliari. — Deadline: March 4, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Rückblende 2026 — German Prize for Political Photography · Landesvertretung Rheinland-Pfalz
item.description: Germany's national prize for political photography asks professional press photographers living in Germany for work on the political year 2026. Entry is free, with a €7,000 first prize, a Leica-funded award for best series and a touring exhibition that runs from Berlin to Bonn, Mainz, Koblenz and Brussels. The portal closes at noon on 30 November, and entries in the best-series category are capped at the first 50. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €7,000 + Exhibition tour + Catalogue.

item.title: NEXT! Festival 2027 — Wir sind doch keine Maschine · Internationale Photoszene Köln
item.description: The youth strand of Cologne's photography festival invites anyone aged 6 to 21 living in Cologne to answer the theme 'Wir sind doch keine Maschine' — we are not machines. Up to five photos, staged, documentary or experimental, no experience needed; selected work hangs at the Rautenstrauch-Joest-Museum from 14 May to 13 June 2027. — Deadline: March 1, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Museum exhibition.

item.title: IRIS — Practices of Relation · Casa degli Artisti
item.description: Casa degli Artisti is selecting ten residencies in Milan exploring how art creates connection between people, open to artists, curators and researchers in any discipline, photography included. Applicants from outside the EU are welcome. The €20,000 support fund is shared across all ten projects, and each one must carry a research component. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency + €20,000 fund.

item.title: National Open Call — Young Photographers · GRAIN Projects
item.description: GRAIN Projects is commissioning one photographer aged 18–26 and living in England to make new work about young people's lives and the challenges they face. The commission pays £2,000, with a further £500 towards a public sharing of the work, plus mentoring. Entry is free, but there is no exhibition and the project runs just eight weeks. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £2,000 commission + Mentoring.

item.title: Chemins de photos 2027 — 14th Edition
item.description: Chemins de photos returns for a 14th edition across some twenty villages of the western Aude, showing selected series as large open-air prints the association pays to produce. No theme, no entry fee, open to any photographer or collective; €30 membership only if selected, and a €300 Jury Prize can reward an unexhibited series. Selected work is licensed non-exclusively for two editions, may be loaned or rented to partners, and is archived online indefinitely. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free (€30 membership if selected). Prize: €500 credit + Exhibition.

item.title: Climate Photo Award 2026
item.description: A new international award for documentary photographs of our changing relationship with the planet, across three categories: climate crisis, biodiversity, and people and land. Winners take €500 for a single image and €1,000 for a series, and winning and finalist work joins a touring exhibition circuit. A binding code of ethics bars composites, generative fill and any altered content; fee waivers can be requested with a justified reason. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: €10/image, €15/series. Prize: €1,500 total + Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Left Coast Annual Juried Exhibition · Sanchez Art Center
item.description: Sanchez Art Center's annual no-theme juried show for artists in California, Oregon, Washington, Alaska and Hawaii, open to all fine-art visual media including photography and video. SFMOMA and MoAD assistant curator Cornelia Stokes juries; selected work hangs in Pacifica from 9 April to 9 May 2027 and online. CaFE entries open 19 November, and two Exhibition Awards add a later show to the $250. — Deadline: January 26, 2027. Fee: $15 per image. Prize: Exhibition + $250 awards.

item.title: BWP x Nikon Grant Fund 2026 — Quarter 4 · Black Women Photographers
item.description: The fourth and final 2026 cycle of Black Women Photographers' grant fund with Nikon, aimed at Black and African women creatives. The recipient receives a $2,500 unrestricted cash grant plus a Nikon Z6III with 24-70mm f/4 lens kit. Applications go through a short form embedded on the page. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $2,500 grant + Nikon Z6III.

item.title: Analog Sparks — International Film Photography Awards 2027
item.description: The 2027 cycle of the international film photography awards, open worldwide to anyone 18 or over across eight categories from Architecture to Technique and Zines & Photo Books. Winners show at House of Lucie galleries in Athens, Ostuni and Budapest. Hybrid analog-digital work is welcome; purely digital is not. — Deadline: July 31, 2027. Fee: €10–€25. Prize: €1,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Aeonian Magazine — Issue No. 15
item.description: Aeonian Magazine is a digital publication for experimental and alternative photography — polaroids, film, cyanotypes, tintypes and lumen prints — now reading for its fifteenth issue. Submissions go by email: five JPEGs plus a short artist statement, with no entry fee. Fourteen issues have appeared since 2020. — Deadline: December 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Eyes of History Student Contest 2027 · White House News Photographers Association
item.description: The Eyes of History student division of the White House News Photographers Association, open to full-time students at any US college and to those who graduated within the year. Winning portfolios travel in the WHNPA exhibition, get a spread in the annual book and a gala invitation in Washington. Entry is $40 and AI-generated images are barred. — Deadline: February 1, 2027. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition + Publication.

item.title: Winston Taylor Irish Photo Prize 2027 · Photo Museum Ireland
item.description: Ireland's largest photography prize returns on the theme Change: a €10,000 first prize, two €2,500 judges' awards and a separate €10,000 bursary for an artist from an underrepresented community. Up to 30 shortlisted artists show at Photo Museum Ireland in Dublin and receive €150 each. Free, but entrants must be based in Ireland or Irish citizens abroad. — Deadline: January 10, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: €30,000 awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Connections: The People and The Place · Josephy Center for Arts & Culture
item.description: Community exhibit at the Josephy Center in Joseph, Oregon on roots, ancestry and lived experience, curated by Chantal Ivenso and open to all artists, with photography named among the accepted categories. Twenty dollars covers three works and under-18s enter free; accepted work must be delivered and collected in person. — Deadline: December 7, 2026. Fee: $20 for up to 3 works (free under 18). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Midwest Award for Artists with Disabilities · Arts Midwest
item.description: Nine unrestricted $3,000 awards, one for each state in Arts Midwest's nine-state region, for mid-career disabled visual artists; photography is named among the eligible 2D media. Applying is free, and the application is three 200-word statements plus three to five work samples. Film and video are not eligible. — Deadline: December 8, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $3,000 grant.

item.title: 2027 Aperture Portfolio Prize
item.description: Aperture's annual international prize for bodies of work not yet widely published or exhibited. The winner takes $5,000, a $1,000 MPB gift card and publication in Aperture; four shortlisted artists get $1,000 each, and all five show at AIPAD New York in April 2027. Entry is free but requires a print subscription. — Deadline: January 6, 2027. Fee: Free (Aperture print subscription required, $75/year). Prize: $5,000 + Exhibition + Publication.

item.title: Betray the Dark · Mosaic Art Collective
item.description: Juried group show at Mosaic Art Collective's Manchester gallery on the darkest season and mental health — grief, resilience, recovery — in any visual medium, photography named. Up to three works at $10 each; the show runs January 2027 and work must be delivered and collected in person. — Deadline: December 18, 2026. Fee: $10–$30. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2028 Artist-in-Residence Program · The Factory on Willow
item.description: The Factory on Willow, a reimagined mill complex in Manchester, New Hampshire, gives emerging artists a live/work studio apartment for up to three months, a $1,600 food and materials stipend, $350 towards travel and a closing solo or duo exhibition. Applying is free and applications are read as they arrive; each resident donates one work made there to the building's collection. — Deadline: October 17, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency + $1,600 stipend + Exhibition.

item.title: Synthetic Truths · UNDERSTORY
item.description: UNDERSTORY, a gallery in Cleveland's 78th Street Studios complex, wants conceptual work about the synthetic, the substitute and the not-quite-real, with photography, installation, audio and new media all welcome. There is no entry fee and no participation fee if you are selected; US artists only, priority within 100 miles of Cleveland. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Trenton Arts Fellowship 2027-28 · Mercer County Community College
item.description: Mercer County Community College and Princeton University's Lewis Center for the Arts name one Trenton Arts Fellow for a 10-month fellowship, September to June, with studio space on the college's Trenton campus, mentorship and a $10,000 stipend and research fund. It is open to visual artists who live and work in the city of Trenton. Applicants must not be enrolled in a programme of study during the fellowship. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Fellowship + $10,000 + Studio space.

item.title: Bluefield Arts Online Festival 2027
item.description: The ninth Bluefield Arts Online Festival shows one work per artist in its online gallery from 21 to 28 February 2027, keeps it up for up to eight months and takes no commission on sales. Awards are honorary and non-monetary, and the form names no jury. Entering grants the festival use of your images for publicity, the gallery and education in perpetuity. — Deadline: January 24, 2027. Fee: $25. Prize: Online exhibition + Honorary awards.

item.title: Experimental Visual Art for Hardcover Book Editions · Point Pleasant Publishing
item.description: Point Pleasant Publishing, a New Jersey Shore art publisher, gives each selected artist a six-page spread with a curatorial review essay in its hardcover catalogue, also published online. It takes experimental work, photography and moving image included, but no AI. Applying is free; selected artists donate at least $55 or buy a paperback, and the $500 tier is a solo monograph in global distribution with 50% of its sales profit to the artist. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free ($55+ donation if selected). Prize: Catalogue essay + Online feature.

item.title: Strasbourg <> Budapest Research and Creation Residency 2027 · CEAAC
item.description: CEAAC's exchange with Budapest Gallery gives one visual artist or curator a month in Budapest in June 2027, with a studio-apartment on Klauzál square, return travel paid and a €1,000 grant from the gallery. Open in all media, at any age or nationality, to early and mid-career applicants who can show a link to France's Grand Est region and are registered under the French artist-author regime. Duos may apply. — Deadline: December 13, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €1,000 grant + Residency + Travel.

item.title: On Absence — 33rd International Studio Program · ACC Galerie Weimar
item.description: The ACC Galerie Weimar and the City of Weimar give three artists four months in Weimar on the theme of absence, with a €1,100 monthly stipend, a rent-free furnished apartment and a 30 m² studio. Open worldwide to artists of any discipline, with no age limit; students cannot apply. Work made there may enter a group show the following year. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €1,100 stipend + Studio.

item.title: Open Call Nacional 2027 · Cultivamos Cultura
item.description: Two 24-week residencies in 2027 for artists of any discipline who are tax resident in Portugal, six weeks of them on site at Cultivamos Cultura's farmhouse in São Luís, Alentejo. Each project carries a €1,600 artist fee, up to €1,250 for production, €12 a day on site and a private room. The work joins the CC collection. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €1,600 fee + Residency.

item.title: Viajantes / OASis Residency 2027 · Cultivamos Cultura
item.description: Mobility residency for Portuguese citizens and residents working across art, research and culture, hosted by Machaon International in Gánovce, Slovakia from 15 to 25 April 2027. The package is a €1,300 artist fee with up to €500 travel, €1,500 accommodation and €1,600 production, and the resident makes work for a collective exhibition. The jury says it is particularly interested in photography, video and documentary storytelling about nature conservation. — Deadline: December 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €1,300 fee + Residency.

item.title: Art For Everyone 2027 · Rena Charles Gallery
item.description: Free community show at Rena Charles Gallery in Healdsburg, California, open to anyone 15 or older working in 2D or 3D media, photography included. There is no jury and no fee: every submission meeting the guidelines hangs in February, capped at one work no larger than ten inches. AI-generated work is not accepted. — Deadline: January 5, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Storm · Kehler Liddell Gallery
item.description: Kehler Liddell Gallery's 11th annual juried show takes storm as noun, verb, metaphor or threat, and accepts work in any medium, photography included. A panel of the New Haven gallery's own artists picks around fifty pieces for a month-long show in Westville. Sales split 60/40 in the artist's favour. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: $35 (up to 3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Forms of Being · CICA Museum
item.description: International group show at CICA Museum in Gimpo, South Korea, on portraits, figures and living forms across photography, printmaking, painting, video, sculpture and installation. Submission is free by email - up to five JPEGs and/or three video links plus a bio. Accepted artists contribute $78 per work toward exhibition processing and maintenance, and the show runs April 28 to May 16, 2027. — Deadline: December 7, 2026. Fee: Free to submit; $78 per accepted work. Prize: Museum exhibition.

item.title: Structures Seen and Unseen · L7 Gallery
item.description: L7 Gallery's international online juried show on structures seen and unseen, from the veins of a leaf to a trestle bridge. Photography is one of eight accepted media, and Greg Robinson, chief curator of the Bainbridge Island Museum of Art, picks a $300 first place plus two honourable mentions. Accepted work must stay for sale for the run of the show, with the gallery taking 40%. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: $30 (1–3 images). Prize: $300 + Exhibition.

item.title: 13th Annual International Open Call · Rhode Island Center for Photographic Arts
item.description: The Rhode Island Center for Photographic Arts clears all its Providence galleries for this no-theme international survey of contemporary photography, open to any process or technology, current or historical. Nick Capasso, director of the Fitchburg Art Museum, is the juror; the top three works take $250, $150 and $75. The gallery keeps 40% on sales. — Deadline: January 23, 2027. Fee: $45 (first 3 images) + $10 per extra image; 20% off for members. Prize: $250 prize + Exhibition.

item.title: 3rd iTravelPoetry Photography Festival
item.description: The third edition of iTravelPoetry's Athens photography festival, on the theme of Christmas, holidays and winter. Selected pictures are printed A3 and hung at the organisation's Chalandri venue for two days, where the public — not a jury — votes the winner a free solo show there plus a place in the Beyond Borders tour. Applying by email is free; €20 per selected photo covers its print. — Deadline: December 13, 2026. Fee: Free (€20 per selected photo, print included). Prize: Solo exhibition + Festival entry.

item.title: The Curated Fridge — Winter 2027 Show
item.description: The Curated Fridge's seasonal no-theme call, juried this round by Joshua Farr of the Vermont Center for Photography, where the show travels in January. Free and open to photographers worldwide, amateur or professional. The catch: you must email JPEGs and also mail actual small prints, postmarked by the deadline. — Deadline: December 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Online feature.

item.title: In View 2027 · The Art Center Highland Park
item.description: The Art Center's annual members-and-faculty show in Highland Park, open to any subject, with photography first on its accepted-media list. Up to three works may be submitted but only one is hung, for a six-week run with a free public reception on 15 January. Work should be for sale and the gallery takes 35%. — Deadline: November 28, 2026. Fee: Free (membership required: $55–$105/year). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Alan Hagman Photojournalism Grant · National Press Photographers Foundation
item.description: A $6,000 grant for professional photojournalists authorized to work in the US or its territories, for underreported stories on human rights, the environment or other pressing social topics; a panel of photojournalism peers judges storytelling, sequencing and ethics. Payment is $5,000 on award and $1,000 on delivery of 25 captioned images within 18 months. The page's status chip reads Closed; its own prose and the live Picter portal run entries to 14 December. — Deadline: December 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $6,000.

item.title: The natural and the artificial · PH21 Gallery
item.description: Curated international group show at PH21's Barcelona gallery on the continuum between the organic and the designed — tamed gardens, abandoned spaces reclaimed by nature, and the frictions where the two meet. Open worldwide to photographers 18 and over, 3 to 15 images submitted by email. Selected photographers pay a €45–€125 print and installation fee. — Deadline: January 4, 2027. Fee: €25–€45 early bird, then €30–€50; €15–€20 concession. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Outdoor Photography Magazine — Winter Mountains
item.description: Outdoor Photography's monthly reader competition takes winter mountains as the theme for issue OP 336. Entrants send up to five images, each with a caption of up to 75 words and the full technical details in the magazine's stated order. Open to readers aged 18 or over, and uploads run through Google Drive, so a Google account is needed. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £159 gear + Publication.

item.title: 2027 Supporting Neurodivergent Creatives · Rotary Club of San Jose
item.description: The Rotary Club of San Jose's grant for neurodivergent artists aged 16 to 25 who live or work in the nine-county Bay Area, with photography explicitly among the eligible forms. Six artists each receive $2,500, and recipients must attend the May 2027 awards ceremony in downtown San Jose in person. — Deadline: February 15, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $2,500 grant.

item.title: Fine Art Awards 2026 · Dodho Magazine
item.description: Dodho Magazine's fine art competition, open worldwide, selects 100 finalists for a 30×30 cm printed annual edition. First, second and third prizes plus two honorable mentions receive a certificate and editorial visibility, and the overall winner is named Photographer of the Year; there is no cash prize. Entry is by paid image pack of three, six or twelve photographs, with VAT added for European entrants. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: €30 (3) / €45 (6) / €60 (12). Prize: Publication + Certificate.

item.title: HOME · Art Fluent
item.description: Art Fluent's online juried exhibit on the theme of home, open worldwide to amateur and professional artists in all fine art media, photography included. Every accepted work is shown in the online gallery; Best of Show wins $750 and two Director's Choice awards $250 each. AI-generated work is not accepted, and work shown in an earlier Art Fluent exhibit cannot be re-entered. — Deadline: February 19, 2027. Fee: $25 + $10 each additional. Prize: $750 + 2×$250.

item.title: PROUD+ 2027 · The Studio Door
item.description: The Studio Door in San Diego holds its tenth PROUD+ exhibition of work by LGBTQ+ artists from 25 June to 6 August 2027, juried by Xiangqi Chen of OUT Museum. Three artists receive a $100 Juror's Award, and all selected work appears in the catalogue. All work must be for sale at 50% commission, and international artists can join the online exhibition only. — Deadline: May 8, 2027. Fee: $35 (1 work), $40 (2), $45 (3). Prize: $100 awards + Exhibition + Catalogue.

item.title: Art of Possibilities Art Show & Sale 2027 · Allina Health Foundation
item.description: The 64th annual juried show for artists with disabilities, at the Courage Kenny Rehabilitation Institute in Minneapolis from 3 June to 9 July 2027, with Photography as one of six categories. Cash awards go to each category and a Best of Show, and artists keep 100% of sales. All work must be for sale; AI-generated work is not accepted. — Deadline: March 15, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Cash awards.

item.title: The Crow Show 2027 · The Studio Door
item.description:
The thirteenth annual national juried exhibition at The Studio Door, the gay-owned and operated gallery Patric Stillman founded in San Diego in 2014, celebrating the crow. The gallery's framing is that the crow has long been a symbol of mystery, transformation and intelligence across cultures, and artists are invited to explore its many faces, whether rooted in reality or soaring through fantasy: creative interpretations of black birds, ravens and other Corvus species are welcome. The call opened 15 November 2026 and the exhibition runs 19 February – 2 April 2027, with two public receptions, on 20 February and 27 March. Walkthrough videos of past editions are on the gallery's YouTube channel.
Each artist may enter up to three works, at $35 for the first and $5 for each additional entry. Submission is through CaFE: one to three JPEGs, at least 1,200 pixels on the longest side and under 5 MB. The accepted media are painting, drawing, photography, printmaking, assemblage, collage, mixed media, fibre art, artist books and sculpture, with oversized jewellery that can be presented as fine art also eligible; performance art is not accepted, and video, film, installation or anything needing mains power requires gallery approval before submission. Framed two-dimensional work must use plexiglass rather than glass because of shipping and may not exceed 60 inches high by 40 inches wide including the frame; sculpture must fit through an average doorway and stay under eight feet. Glass and ceramic works are accepted only if hand-delivered. Patric Stillman is the sole juror; he served on the jury of the Oceanside Museum of Art's 2025 Biennial and writes a monthly arts column for The WORD San Diego.
Three artists each receive a $100 Juror's Award for imaginative and compelling interpretations of the theme, judged on originality, execution, emotional impact and interpretation. The juror selects works for the physical gallery and further works for an online gallery, and applicants choose which they want to be considered for; online-only selections are equally eligible for Best in Show. The gallery calls this a national exhibition based in the United States, and because of shipping costs, tariffs and customs, international artists may take part in the online exhibition only, with international sales handled by the gallery. All selected work, in gallery or online, appears in the exhibition catalogue, available online and print-on-demand. Jury review runs 17–21 January with notification on 22 January 2027. All work must be for sale, with the gallery retaining 50 per cent and commission cheques mailed within 30 days of closing; artists cover shipping and supply prepaid return labels. — Deadline: January 16, 2027. Fee: $35 (1 work), $40 (2), $45 (3). Prize: $100 awards + Exhibition + Catalogue.

item.title: GRANDEUR OF COLOR · MVA Gallery
item.description:
MVA Gallery, a commercial gallery in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, runs a rolling programme of themed national group shows, and this one takes colour as its subject. The gallery's framing is that colour is everywhere and exerts a powerful influence on perception, emotion and behaviour, and that an artist's use of it is personal — intellectual or intuitive, purposeful or accidental, traditional or experimental. Some artists depict the perceived relationship between colours and objects faithfully; others inhabit a subjective universe where colour is relative, transferring shapes and transforming objects to reconstruct reality. Work may be realistic or imaginary, representational or abstract, with no restrictions on subject matter or style. The show occupies both of the gallery's exhibition rooms, 5–30 May 2027, with accepted work due at the gallery by 30 April 2027.
The gallery accepts painting, watercolour, printmaking, mixed media, digital, pastel, encaustic, ink, sculpture, fibre, drawing and photography, and states that all photographic processes are welcome. Photographs should be framed for a traditional presentation, with black or white frames preferred and white or off-white mats where used, though other mounting is considered and exceptions are made. There is no cut-off date for when the work was made. Work must not exceed 48 inches framed on the longest side or 50 lbs, must carry a stretched wire for hanging, and must not have been shown at MVA before. Entry is $35 for three different images and $5 for each additional file up to a maximum of nine; submission runs through CaFE only. Images must be JPEG, under 5 MB and at least 1,200 pixels on the longest side. Work may be offered for sale, with 70 per cent of any sale price going to the artist and 30 per cent to the gallery, and artists pay shipping and insurance both ways and must enclose a prepaid UPS or FedEx return label. A small rotating committee of artists, gallerists, art reviewers, publishers, curators and academics reviews the work, and its decisions are final.
Three awards are in play. An Art of Distinction award selects one artist, photographer or sculptor for a featured show in the gallery's Exhibition Room Two at a future date. The Director's Choice Award is $200, granted at the executive director's discretion. The annual Grand Prize goes to one artist chosen from everyone exhibited at MVA across the calendar year, who is offered an exhibition opportunity in New York City. Artists in a further category are granted free submission to a future MVA exhibition. Notification is by email on or about 4 March 2027, with separate messages for invited and not-invited entries and no acknowledgement of applications before then. The call is national: artists must be 18 or older and current residents of the United States. — Deadline: November 29, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: REFLECTIONS · Kunsthalle Burkamp
item.description:
Kunsthalle Burkamp in Haltern am See is assembling a group exhibition on the theme REFLECTIONS, planned for 2 May to 18 July 2027 with a vernissage. The theme spans reflection as an optical phenomenon and reflection as inner, mental movement: mirrorings on shimmering materials, water, glass, light and shadow, and images caught between visibility, likeness and illusion — and also RE-FLECTIONS as echo, the return of memories, emotions and historical traces that change in the retelling. The building is a former Haltern glassworks, and the call makes a point of that history: glass, both transparent and reflective, is meant to carry particular weight in the show.
The call is open to artists of all ages; no particular training or exhibition record is required. Media named as welcome include painting, drawing, sculpture and photography, as well as other forms suited to the spaces, but large-format installations, film and elaborate projections cannot be realised for technical reasons. Both existing works and concepts for new production may be submitted. Each application may carry 1 to 10 works. Selection is made by the Kunsthalle's curatorial team, and selected artists are contacted around the turn of the year 2026/27.
There is no application fee. Artists who are selected pay a participation fee towards the exhibition's costs, expected to be €150–€350 depending on how much external funding the Kunsthalle secures, with the exact figure given on acceptance. Artists deliver their work to Haltern am See themselves; installation and deinstallation are handled by the Kunsthalle team or jointly with the artist, and the Kunsthalle organises sales. Material needed for presentation — plinths, framing for photographs — is the artist's to provide after consultation.
Applications go by email as a single PDF containing a statement on the work and its relation to the theme (max. one A4 page), images with title, year, medium and dimensions, a short self-introduction for artists new to the Kunsthalle, and any special technical requirements. — Deadline: November 21, 2026. Fee: Free (€150–€350 participation fee if selected). Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Open Call for Exhibitions 2027 · Valokuvakeskus Peri
item.description:
Valokuvakeskus Peri (Photographic Centre Peri) is one of Finland's seven regional photography centres, working in photography and lens-based contemporary art from the Kilta Gallery in Art House Turku, a former fire station at Nunnankatu 4. It is now seeking exhibition proposals for its 2027 programme from artists, collectives and curators working professionally in those fields, and says it particularly wants to highlight the work of underrepresented artists and topics that have had little or no attention in the Finnish art field.
The economics are stated plainly and in the artist's favour: Peri does not charge a gallery rental fee, and it pays an exhibition fee to every exhibitor. The number of shows is deliberately limited so that each artist can be paid properly — four exhibition periods of roughly seven weeks, with one or two exhibitions selected for each, the first opening to the public on 7 May 2027. Artists are part of the working community during installation and deinstallation, and the centre provides production support.
The gallery is three rooms totalling 228.5 m² (107, 66 and 55.5 m², the last able to be darkened); partition walls take works almost anywhere, the ceiling has regular bolt points, and the street-facing stone window walls cannot be hung. Peri also says it wants to reduce unpaid application work: a proposal does not need to be production-ready, and its degree of finish is not itself a selection criterion.
Proposals go through an online form with a PDF of the proposal and work samples (under 50 MiB) plus a CV. The jury is exhibition curator Maria Huokkola, photographic artist Emma Sarpaniemi and senior university lecturer in photography and author Hanna Weselius; the director takes part in the process to check each proposal is feasible with Peri's resources, and jury members declare conflicts of interest and stand aside on those proposals. The director also keeps open telephone hours during the application period, 10:00–12:00 on Friday 20 November 2026. — Deadline: December 4, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Artist fee.
